findings.title: A coverage range at the populated span's edge exits 4 as "database unreachable"
findings.description: `build_coverage` asks the calendar for `[utc_midnight(start - timedelta(days=1)), utc_midnight(end))` (lines 103-104) so a session that opens the previous evening is included. `TradingCalendar.sessions_between` calls `_require_populated` on **both** bounds (`data/base/trading_calendar.py:310-317`), and `calendar_sessions` (`tick_status_build.py:63-75`) converts `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` into `TickCalendarError`. `exit_code_for` maps `TickCalendarError` to `EXIT_STORAGE` (`cli/commands/tick_exit.py`), so `mt data tick coverage --start <first populated session date>` — a legitimate request — prints the calendar's "outside calendar … Run 'mt data extend'" refusal and exits **4**, which `READ_EPILOG` (`tick_store_cmds.py:37-42`) documents as "the tick or production (calendar) database is unreachable." The operator gets a storage-outage diagnosis and a storage exit code for what is an out-of-range input. Either clamp the lookback to the populated span's first open, or map this refusal to exit 1 and say so in the epilog. (The share of this that is genuinely a storage outage — a dead connection — already reaches exit 4 through `psycopg.OperationalError`.)

findings.title: `caught_up` is computed on a different condition than the `wanted` range it reports on
findings.description: The in-scope `wanted` tuple is built at lines 187-192 and is `None` whenever `_wanted_end` cannot produce an end (`entry.end is None` **and** no `tick_dataset_edge` row — `_wanted_end`, lines 140-144). But the `caught_up` flag at line 217 tests only `wanted_start is not None`. So a product with `tier` set but an unknown/absent dataset edge falls into `_scope`'s held-units-only branch (no wanted bounds added, line 158), yet reports `caught up: yes/no` instead of the `n/a` that `caught_up`'s own docstring reserves for "the product has no wanted range" (`tick_status.py`, `caught_up`). Concretely, it can print `caught up: yes` over a scope that contains only days already held, which is precisely the reading TD9's "n/a (no wanted range)" branch exists to prevent. Today `TICK_UNIVERSE` has `tier=None`, so this is latent until 226 sets a tier — but it is the state 226 immediately lands in. Keying the flag off `wanted is not None` (the same value used for scope) makes the two agree.

findings.title: Spreads are hidden by dataclass equality rather than by class
findings.description: `[c for c in lines if c not in spreads]` relies on `ContractLine` being a frozen dataclass whose `__eq__` compares every field, including the mutable-by-content `sessions`/`records`/`volume` counters. It is correct only because `instrument_id` is unique per line. `c.instrument_class != SPREAD_CLASS` — the same constant used four lines earlier to build `spreads` (line 198) — states the rule directly and needs no reasoning about equality semantics.

findings.title: `_DATE_FORMAT` is redefined instead of shared
findings.description: `_DATE_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%d"` duplicates the identical constant in `cli/commands/tick.py:51`, and the two define the accepted CLI date format for the same command group. The project rule is explicit that a comparison value should be defined once and referenced everywhere; `tick_store_cmds.py` already imports from `tick_exit.py`, so a shared constant there (or a single module-level one) costs nothing. The same applies to the repeated `typer.Option(False, "--json", …)` definition, though that predates this slice.

findings.title: `_read_storage()` is an indirection that returns a constant
findings.description: The function exists only to defer one import and is called at both call sites (lines 201 and 236) to produce the same one-element tuple. Inlining `(TickDatabaseUnreachable,)` at the `run_mapped(..., storage=...)` call removes a level of indirection with no behaviour change.

findings.title: Float division converts nanosecond expiries to dates
findings.description: `datetime.fromtimestamp(c.expiration_ns / 1e9, UTC)` goes through a double for an integer-nanosecond value, in a renderer whose whole job is displaying them. It matches the precedent at `ingest_checks.py:31`, so it is not novel, but the exact idiom used elsewhere in the tick package (`// timedelta(microseconds=1)`, `ingest_records.utc_ns`) is available and cannot round.

findings.title: Status re-runs the same unit query twice per product
findings.description: `_product_status` calls `_scope`, which calls `shape_units` (line 155), and then `session_verdicts`, which calls `shape_units` again (line 87) — the identical query with the identical parameters. Both feed the same product's report. The table is small today, so this is not a hot-path problem, but it is a duplicated read that a single call threaded through would remove.

findings.title: The new renderer's pure helpers carry no direct test
findings.description: `age()` — including the "largest two units" truncation and the `0m` / `hours == 0` branches — and `_label()` have no direct test; the renderer is exercised only end-to-end through `test/integration/data/test_tick_status_cli.py`, which asserts the complete-note and spreads strings but never an age or label. These are pure functions with three branches each and would be cheap to parametrize, in the style `test/unit/data/tick/test_tick_status.py` already uses for the classification table.

findings.title: Day-tiling logic is now stated once
findings.description: The slice replaces `ingest_plan._midnight` with the shared `utc_midnight` and lifts `session_days`' inline day walk into `days_touched`, which `tick_status_build` then reuses for scope, verdicts and coverage. I traced the reformulation of `session_days` (`touched.update(...)` with the `start <= day < end` filter moving out of the loop) against the previous behaviour in the diff and the existing unit tests in `test/unit/data/tick/test_session_days.py` — the clipping order changes but the result does not.

findings.title: New destructive statements are confined to fixture-created databases
findings.description: The two `DELETE FROM tick_trade …` statements in the new tests (also `test_tick_status_cli.py:125-128`) take their connection from `migrated_tick_db`, which `test/conftest.py` builds via the `mt_test_t` throwaway-database context manager and drops on teardown. Neither file reads `MT_TICK_DB_URL` or `MT_TIMESCALE_DB_URL`; the closed-port URL in `test_tick_status_cli.py:39-42` is constructed in-test. This satisfies the production-protection rules, and the delete-by-primary-key comment (rather than `ctid`) matches the guidance recorded in the slice's walkthrough.
